propositions: Plans assert that named modules provide or lack specific capabilities, but those assertions are false against actual code (module exists but capability absent, or capability exists but plan says absent)
The existing E4 code-grounding probe misses capability-surface mismatches because it only checks module existence, not the finer-grained capability surface
A new advisory, code-grounded, agentic plan-review criterion must detect when a plan's capability claims about named modules are refuted by the codebase
The criterion must register as non-orphan advisory in registry and routing, include a rubric prompt and guide section, and pass deterministic unit tests and bounded sanity checks
The criterion must auto-flow into the standing effectiveness recorder with zero per-criterion wiring and remain advisory until promoted to blocking via the promotion gate
The bounded sanity check must demonstrate >=66% recall over the 3 E1-verified misses with no blocking false positives on clean plans
